quality_assessment: Page has critical factual error about DFA size limit default value (off by 1000x). Otherwise comprehensive and well-structured with excellent visual diagrams.

issues.description: Documentation states default DFA size limit is 1 MB (1000000 bytes), but actual default is 1000 MB (1,048,576,000 bytes) - off by 1000x
issues.current_content: The default is 1 MB (1000000 bytes). Increase this if you see warnings about DFA cache thrashing on very large or complex patterns.
issues.should_be: The default is 1000 MB (approximately 1 GB). Increase this if you see warnings about DFA cache thrashing on very large or complex patterns.
issues.fix_suggestion: Update line 263 to reflect the actual default DFA size limit of 1000 MB. The code shows: `dfa_size_limit: 1000 * (1 << 20)` which equals 1,048,576,000 bytes (1000 MB, not 1 MB).

issues.description: Documentation suggests increasing to 10M or 100M, but default is already 1000M - recommendation should be revised
issues.current_content: If you see "DFA cache capacity exceeded" warnings or notice slowdowns with complex patterns, try increasing to 10M or 100M. The trade-off is higher memory usage for faster matching.
issues.should_be: If you see "DFA cache capacity exceeded" warnings (rare with the 1000 MB default), you can increase further to 2G or more. The trade-off is higher memory usage for faster matching.
issues.fix_suggestion: Update the tip box starting at line 265 to provide realistic tuning guidance given the 1000 MB default. Suggest values larger than the default if users need to increase it.

issues.description: Documentation says 'default is 100 MB' without clarifying this is compiled regex bytecode size, not DFA cache
issues.current_content: The default is 100 MB. Useful in memory-constrained environments or when dealing with extremely large patterns.
issues.should_be: The default is 100 MB (104,857,600 bytes) for the compiled regex bytecode size. This is separate from the DFA cache limit. Useful in memory-constrained environments or when dealing with extremely large patterns.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add clarification at line 277 that this controls the compiled regex bytecode size, not the DFA cache size, to avoid confusion between --regex-size-limit and --dfa-size-limit.
